We need to produce test cases for exception scenarios of isLessThan method. The existing test cases already include a null argument handling case expecting NullPointerException. Need to analyze method: return new UnderIndicatorRule(this, other). UnderIndicatorRule likely throws NullPointerException if other is null. Also maybe if this.delegate is null? NumericIndicator wraps delegate; but constructor requires delegate non-null? Not shown. Could be that passing a NumericIndicator whose delegate is null leads to NPE later. But method uses 'this' as first argument; UnderIndicatorRule may check both non-null. So exception scenarios: null other; maybe other indicator returns null Num at some index causing NPE inside rule evaluation? However isLessThan itself just creates rule; not evaluate. So only exception at creation time: NullPointerException if other is null. Also maybe IllegalArgumentException if other is not of same type? UnderIndicatorRule expects Indicator<Num>, so compile-time ensures. So only null.

But instruction: "Identify ALL possible exception scenarios". Could also be that this delegate is null causing NPE in UnderIndicatorRule's constructor when it accesses other.getBarSeries? Not sure. But we can create test case where NumericIndicator.of(null) returns NumericIndicator with null delegate, then call isLessThan(other). That may cause NPE. However of() method likely throws IllegalArgumentException if delegate null. Not known.

Given we need to avoid duplication; existing test already has null argument handling. So maybe there are no other exception scenarios, thus we return empty array? But we must output test cases for uncovered exception scenarios. Since only null other is covered, maybe there is also scenario where other indicator is of mismatched BarSeries leading to IllegalArgumentException? UnderIndicatorRule may require same BarSeries; if not, it may throw IllegalArgumentException. So we can test passing other indicator built from different BarSeries; expect IllegalArgumentException. Also maybe passing other indicator that is not numeric? but type is Indicator<Num>. So not.

Thus we add test group "NumericIndicator.isLessThan - mismatched series handling". Input: other = ConstantIndicator(5) built with a different BarSeries than the NumericIndicator's series. Expected: throws IllegalArgumentException (or maybe IllegalArgumentException). Need to be safe: UnderIndicatorRule constructor checks series equality and throws IllegalArgumentException if not same. We'll assume.

Also scenario: passing other indicator that throws exception when getValue called (e.g., custom indicator that throws RuntimeException). But isLessThan just constructs rule; rule evaluation may later cause exception, but method itself doesn't. However test could call rule.isSatisfied and expect exception. That would be exception scenario for rule evaluation, not method. The instruction is for focal method isLessThan, not rule evaluation. So only creation.

Thus we add one new group for mismatched series.

If there are no other scenarios, we output JSON with that group.
